title: Archiphonemes and the glottal stop
description: An archiphoneme is a sound that an underlying form carries and a rule changes. The nasal of a prefix such as paN- is one example: it is m, n or ng by the sound after it, and never N. LibLCM has no archiphoneme flag, and neither HermitCrab nor PanGloss treats one specially. It is a plain phoneme, so Motif authors it with Author a phoneme like any other.
